---
title: Private threads, authors and message metadata
description: "Thread visibility in Pi Durable Platform's API, how the platform sets message authors and tells the agent who speaks, participants, and the metadata on each message."
---

## Visibility

A thread is `shared` or `private`, chosen **when it starts**. Three things start a thread, and the first one to happen chooses:

- `POST /v1/agents/{agentId}/threads` with `{"visibility": "private"}`, which also gives you an ID nobody can guess ([Start a thread](/docs/build/threads-and-messages#start-a-thread));
- its first message, with `visibility`:

  ```json
  {"text": "Draft my performance review", "requestId": "r1", "visibility": "private"}
  ```

- setting its [MCP servers](/docs/build/thread-mcp-servers), with `visibility` in the body of the `PUT`.

When none says, the thread is shared.

- **Shared** (the default): everyone who may use the agent sees it, sends to it and follows it.
- **Private**: only the person or service account that started it. On every thread route (read, send, stop, events, rename, delete, thread MCP servers), in lists and in event streams, someone else's private thread answers `404 thread_not_found`, exactly like a thread that doesn't exist.

Later requests may omit `visibility`. It never changes: a different value is `409 visibility_fixed`, whichever of the three sent it.

The platform writes the thread's record (creator and visibility) when the thread starts, **before** relaying the first message, so a private thread is never briefly shared. Threads from before the platform kept records, which it learns of from the agent, count as shared.

For a person's own conversations with a **team's** agent, send `private`. In a personal workspace only its owner reaches the agent, so shared is fine there.

### What private threads don't hide

A private thread hides a conversation from other callers. It doesn't partition the agent: every thread of an agent has the same instructions, model and MCP servers, and those servers act with the same credentials in every thread, so anything they store is shared. There is no memory across threads and no shared filesystem. If users must have nothing in common, give each one an agent ([Agents for your app's users](/docs/build/agents-by-key)).

Platform admins can still read any conversation by stating a reason, which is recorded in the team's audit log ([Reading conversations](/docs/administer/reading-conversations)).

## Authors

The platform sets each user message's `author` from the credential and ignores any author a client sends:

```json
{"kind": "user", "id": "…", "name": "Sam Ortiz", "via": "Example Corp Chat"}
```

- `kind` is `user` or `service_account`; `name` is the person's display name (else email) or the service account's name.
- `via` is the app's name when a person sent it through OAuth Connect.
- Since v0.4, `kind` can also be `trigger`: a message a [schedule or webhook](/docs/teams/triggers) sent, with the trigger's `id` and `name`. The model is told `[Message from trigger <name>]`. A trigger's thread is shared and started by nobody (`createdBy` is null).

On **shared** threads of a shared team's agent, the model is told who is speaking: its copy of each message starts with a line `[Message from <name>]`. Personal workspaces and private threads don't add it.

Threads list `createdBy` (who started it) and `participants` (everyone who has sent to it, first sender first, each with `lastSentAt`).

## Message metadata

Messages in a conversation view carry:

| Field | On | |
|---|---|---|
| `id`, `role` | all | `user`, `assistant` or `tool` |
| `text`, `thinking` | user, assistant | |
| `author` | user | Above |
| `at` | user, assistant | When it was sent, or when the reply started (Unix ms) |
| `model` | assistant | `{provider, id}` |
| `usage` | assistant | `input`, `output`, `cacheRead`, `cacheWrite`, `total` tokens |
| `stopReason` | assistant | `stop`, `length`, `toolUse`, `error` or `aborted` |
| `error` | assistant | A reply that failed or was interrupted |
| `toolCalls` | assistant | `id`, `name`, `arguments`, `startedAt`, `endedAt` (absent while it runs), and `approval` once a person's approval was asked for it ([Tool approvals](/docs/teams/tool-approvals)) |
| `toolCallId`, `name`, `isError` | tool | The result of a tool call |
| `details`, `detailsOmitted` | tool | Structured data the tool returned for apps, at most 16 KiB ([Agent state for apps](/docs/build/agent-state)) |

Older messages have what was recorded then. The live parts of the view (`partial` and `tools`) don't carry these fields: to time a running tool, match `tools[].callId` with `toolCalls[].id` in `messages`, where the call normally already has `startedAt`.
